a)The above unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026. have been prepared considering the requirements of regulation 33 of the Securities and Exchange board of India (Listing obligations and disclosure requirements) Regulations 2015, as amended. These results have been reviewed by the Audit committee in their meeting held on 10th Nov, 2026 and approved by the board of directors on the same date.
b)The unaudited finandial results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026 have been prepared in accordance with the Indian Accounting Standards (Ind-AS) as prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013,The Statutory Auditors of the Company have carried out limited review of these standalone financial results.For more details on the Unaudited Financials Results visit 'Investor Relations' section of our website at www. quadrantfuturetek.com and Financial Results' in Corporates” section of www.nseindia.com and www.bseindia com
c)The Company has completed its Initial Public Offer (IPO) comprised of fresh issue of 1,00,00,000 equity shares of face value Rs. 10 each at an issue price of Rs. 290 per share (including a share premium of Rs. 280 per share) and as a result the equity shares of the Company were listed on National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited (BSE) on 14th January 2025.
d)Company operates in two segments, i.e., (a) manufacturing of speciality cable and (b) manufacturing of Train control systems.
e)Previous years figures have been regrouped, re-arranged and re-classifed wherever necessary to confirm to current period's classification.
f)EPS and DEPS for the respective periods have been calculated based on the weighted average number of shares outstanding for the said periods.
On 09.07.2026, the stock options granted to employees covered under the Company's Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP), were forfeited and the corresponding share-based payment expenses were reversed, in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 102, Share-based Payment.
Consequently, the number of potential equity shares considered for the computation of Diluted Earnings Per Share (DEPS) for the comparative period has been revised to reflect the reduction in dilutive potential equity shares arising from the forfeiture of the aforesaid stock options. Accordingly, the comparative DEPS figures and EPS figures have been restated, wherever applicable.
g)During the current period, the Company has reassessed the presentation of retention money balances previously classified under Non-Current Trade Receivables and reclassified the same under Other Financial Assets under Non Current Assets, considering the nature of such balances and the contractual terms governing their recovery. Retention money represents amounts withheld by customers, which are recoverable upon fulfilment of specified contractual conditions and are therefore presented separately as financial assets. This reclassification is a change in presentation and does not affect the recognition, measurement or carrying value of the balances or the Company's profit for the period.
h)During the half year ended 30 September 2026, the Company incurred a cash loss of Rs. 79.37 million, compared with Rs. 25.71 million for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 and Rs. 310.22 million in the previous financial year. The losses primarily reflect upfront investments made during the pre-commercialisation phase of the KAVACH project, including expenditure on research and development, employee costs, equipment, materials, engineering, validation and project execution. Such expenditure is strategic in nature and aligns with the Company’s long-term business objectives and the execution of its existing order book. The Train Control Systems Division remains in a pre-commercial investment phase, with costs being incurred ahead of the conversion of the KAVACH order book, valued at Rs. 8,054 million, into billed revenue; accordingly, the losses primarily reflect the timing of project execution and the related investment ahead of revenue recognition. The Company’s net worth, relatively low reliance on borrowings and healthy order book support management’s assessment that these losses do not, in themselves, cast doubt on the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern. Based on its assessment of the Company’s operational and financial position, management believes that the Company has adequate resources to continue its operations, realize its assets and discharge its liabilities in the ordinary course of business. Accordingly, these financial results have been prepared on a going concern basis.
